saints.name: St. Teresa Benedicta of the Cross
saints.title: Virgin and Martyr
saints.shortBlurb: The Jewish philosopher Edith Stein, who became a Carmelite nun and died at Auschwitz, a co-patroness of Europe…
biography: Edith Stein was born at Breslau in 1891, the youngest of eleven children of an observant Jewish family, her birthday falling on the Day of Atonement. A gifted philosopher, she took her doctorate summa cum laude under Edmund Husserl at Freiburg in 1916 and became his assistant.

Reading the autobiography of Teresa of Ávila in 1921, she declared, 'This is the truth,' and was baptized a Catholic on 1 January 1922. After years of teaching at Speyer, she entered the Discalced Carmelites at Cologne in 1933, taking the name Teresa Benedicta of the Cross.

For her safety she was sent in 1938 to the Carmel of Echt in the Netherlands with her sister Rosa. When the Dutch bishops publicly condemned Nazi racism in July 1942, the regime arrested Catholics of Jewish descent in reprisal; seized on 2 August, she was killed in a gas chamber at Auschwitz on 9 August 1942.

Beatified in 1987 and canonized in 1998 by John Paul II, she was declared a co-patroness of Europe in 1999. A daughter of Israel who offered her life for her people and a convert who found Christ, she is honoured as patroness of Europe and of converts.
saints.knownFor: Uniting Jewish heritage, philosophy, and Carmelite martyrdom.

canonization.canonized: 1998 by Pope John Paul II; co-patroness of Europe (1999)
